chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the ornaments, 'Is there Zakat regarding it?' He said: 'No'.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْحُلِيِّ: Ornaments/Jewelry (specifically gold and silver items worn)

ai.seo_question: Is Zakat due on gold and silver jewelry?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that Zakat is not obligatory on personal jewelry (al-huliy), distinguishing it from trade goods or stored wealth. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that ornaments intended for personal use and adornment are exempt from the annual alms tax, provided they do not exceed the nisab threshold for their material value in a manner that transforms them into capital assets. The narration underscores the distinction between consumption/use and accumulation in Islamic fiscal law.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I asked himasws about the ornaments, ‘Is there Zakāt regarding it?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from ibn Muskan from Muhammad al- Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about Zakat and jewelry.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Zakat is not due on jewelries.’”
